'''''Brachypodium''''' (short foot) is a [[genus]] of plants in the [[Poaceae|grass family]], widespread across much of [[Africa]], [[Eurasia]], and [[Latin America]].<ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/393998#page/184/mode/1up Palisot de Beauvois, Ambroise Marie François Joseph. 1812. Essai d'une Nouvelle Agrostographie 100-101] in Latin</ref><ref>[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/393998#page/304/mode/1up Palisot de Beauvois, Ambroise Marie François Joseph. 1812. Essai d'une Nouvelle Agrostographie plante XIX (19)], figure III (3 a-f) line drawings of ''Brachypodium pinnatum''</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=20767 Flora of China, Vol. 22 Page 368 <big>短柄草族</big> duan bing cao zu Poaceae Tribe Brachypodieae ]</ref><ref>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=5&taxon_id=104468 Flora of Pakistan, ''Brachypodium'' P. Beauv.]</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Brachypodium Altervista Flora Italiana, genere ''Brachypodium'']</ref><ref>[http://redlist.sanbi.org/genus.php?genus=1160 Sanbi Red List of South African Plants]</ref> The genus is classified in its own tribe '''Brachypodieae'''.<ref name="SorengPeterson2017">{{cite journal|last1=Soreng|first1=Robert J.|last2=Peterson|first2=Paul M.|last3=Romaschenko|first3=Konstantin|last4=Davidse|first4=Gerrit|last5=Teisher|first5=Jordan K.|last6=Clark|first6=Lynn G.|last7=Barberá|first7=Patricia|last8=Gillespie|first8=Lynn J.|last9=Zuloaga|first9=Fernando O.|title=A worldwide phylogenetic classification of the Poaceae (Gramineae) II: An update and a comparison of two 2015 classifications|journal=Journal of Systematics and Evolution|volume=55|issue=4|year=2017|pages=259–290|issn=1674-4918|doi=10.1111/jse.12262|doi-access=free|hdl=10261/240149|hdl-access=free}} {{open access}}</ref>

Flimsy upright stems form [[tussock (grass)|tussock]]s. Flowers appear in compact spike-like racemes with 5-25 flowers on each short-stalked spikelet in summer. Leaves are flat or curved.<ref>{{cite web|url= http://delta-intkey.com/grass/www/brachypo.htm |title=The grass genera of the world: descriptions, illustrations, identification, and information retrieval; including synonyms, morphology, anatomy, physiology, phytochemistry, cytology, classification, pathogens, world and local distribution, and references |access-date=2009-08-19 |author=Watson L, Dallwitz MJ. |year=2008 |work=The Grass Genera of the World }}</ref><ref>Lord, Tony (2003) Flora : The Gardener's Bible : More than 20,000 garden plants from around the world. London: Cassell. {{ISBN|0-304-36435-5}}</ref>

According to a study published in 2010, there is evidence of ''Brachypodium'' and cattail (''[[Typha]]'' spp.) residues occurring on prehistoric human grinding tools dated 28,000 years ago from Bilancino in central Italy.<ref>{{cite news|last=Callaway|first=Ewen|title=Stone Age flour found across Europe|url=http://www.nature.com/news/2010/101018/full/news.2010.549.html|access-date=October 12, 2011|newspaper=naturenews|date=October 18, 2010}}</ref> Another contemporaneously published study stated that the grain residues resemble ''Brachypodium'', based on a comparison to two modern specimens: "Among these, the grains, which are slightly angular, with hardly visible centric, point-shaped hila and adequate dimensions (in the sample measuring 9–14 μm), appeared very similar to those of ''Brachypodium'' or related genera."<ref>{{cite journal|last=Revedin|first=Anna|title=Thirty thousand-year-old evidence of plant food processing|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|date=November 2, 2010|volume=107|issue=44|pages=18815–18819|doi=10.1073/pnas.1006993107|pmid=20956317|pmc=2973873|bibcode=2010PNAS..10718815R|display-authors=etal|doi-access=free}}</ref>
